blocks.en: 1. The Genealogy from Adam to Noah: Ten Generations of Mercy
blocks.es_reference: 1. La Genealogía de Adán a Noé: Diez Generaciones de Misericordia

blocks.en: Genesis 5 traces ten generations from Adam to Noah. The list looks tedious — but every name in it is a quiet sermon. God did not give up on humanity after the Fall. Through judgment came preservation; through death came a continuing line of those who would call upon His name. The lifespans recorded — Adam 930 years, Methuselah 969 years, Lamech 777 — strain modern credulity but reflect a creation still nearer its original integrity. Even after sin, decay had not yet finished its work. The genealogy ends with Noah, born to Lamech (not Cain's Lamech — a different man entirely). At Noah's birth, his father prophesied: "This one will comfort us concerning our work and the toil of our hands, because of the ground which the Lord has cursed."
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 5 traza diez generaciones desde Adán hasta Noé. La lista parece tediosa — pero cada nombre en ella es un sermón silencioso. Dios no abandonó a la humanidad después de la Caída. A través del juicio vino la preservación; a través de la muerte vino una línea continua de aquellos que invocarían Su nombre. Los lapsos de vida registrados — Adán 930 años, Matusalén 969 años, Lamec 777 — tensan la credulidad moderna pero reflejan una creación aún cercana a su integridad original. Aun después del pecado, la decadencia no había terminado su obra. La genealogía termina con Noé, nacido de Lamec (no el Lamec de Caín — un hombre diferente por completo). Al nacer Noé, su padre profetizó: "Éste nos aliviará de nuestras obras y del trabajo de nuestras manos, a causa de la tierra que Jehová maldijo".

blocks.en: 2. Enoch: He Walked with God
blocks.es_reference: 2. Enoc: Caminó con Dios

blocks.en: Buried in Genesis 5 is one of the most remarkable verses in Scripture. Of every other patriarch in the list, Moses writes, "and he died." But of Enoch: "Enoch walked with God; and he was not, for God took him." Enoch did not die. He was translated — taken bodily into God's presence at age 365. This single verse, set into a chapter on mortality, declares that the grave is not the final word. Centuries before any explicit doctrine of resurrection, God shows His people that fellowship with Him does not end at death. The New Testament will pick up this verse (Hebrews 11:5) as proof that "without faith it is impossible to please Him."
blocks.es_reference: Enterrado en Génesis 5 hay uno de los versículos más notables de la Escritura. De cada otro patriarca en la lista, Moisés escribe "y murió". Pero de Enoc: "Y caminó Enoc con Dios, y desapareció, porque le llevó Dios". Enoc no murió. Fue trasladado — llevado corporalmente a la presencia de Dios a los 365 años. Este versículo único, colocado en un capítulo sobre la mortalidad, declara que la tumba no es la palabra final. Siglos antes de cualquier doctrina explícita de resurrección, Dios muestra a Su pueblo que la comunión con Él no termina en la muerte. El Nuevo Testamento retomará este versículo (Hebreos 11:5) como prueba de que "sin fe es imposible agradar a Dios".

blocks.en: Genesis 5:24 (NKJV): "And Enoch walked with God; and he was not, for God took him."
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 5:24 (RVG): "Y caminó Enoc con Dios, y desapareció, porque le llevó Dios."

blocks.en: 3. The Wickedness of Humanity
blocks.es_reference: 3. La Maldad de la Humanidad

blocks.en: Genesis 6 opens with one of Scripture's most debated passages. "The sons of God saw the daughters of men, that they were beautiful; and they took wives for themselves of all whom they chose." The phrase "sons of God" (bene elohim) is used elsewhere in the Old Testament to refer to angelic beings (Job 1:6, 2:1, 38:7). The most natural reading — and the one Jewish and early Christian interpreters held — is that fallen angels took human wives, producing the Nephilim, "fallen ones," a hybrid race of unusual power. Jude and 2 Peter both seem to confirm this reading. Whatever the precise interpretation, the result is clear: humanity had so corrupted itself that "every intent of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually." God grieved that He had made man on the earth.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 6 abre con uno de los pasajes más debatidos de la Escritura. "Los hijos de Dios vieron que las hijas de los hombres eran hermosas, y tomaron para sí esposas, escogiendo entre todas". La frase "hijos de Dios" (bene elohim) se usa en otras partes del Antiguo Testamento para referirse a seres angélicos (Job 1:6, 2:1, 38:7). La lectura más natural — y la que sostuvieron los intérpretes judíos y cristianos primitivos — es que ángeles caídos tomaron esposas humanas, produciendo a los Nefilim, "caídos", una raza híbrida de poder inusual. Tanto Judas como 2 Pedro parecen confirmar esta lectura. Cualquiera sea la interpretación precisa, el resultado es claro: la humanidad se había corrompido tanto que "todo designio de los pensamientos del corazón de ellos era de continuo solamente el mal". A Dios le dolió haber hecho al hombre en la tierra.

blocks.en: 4. Noah Found Grace
blocks.es_reference: 4. Noé Halló Gracia

blocks.en: Then comes one of the most beautiful verses in the Old Testament: "But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord." This is the first occurrence of the word grace (Hebrew chen) in the Bible. Not earned. Not deserved. Found. Noah did not climb up to God; God's favor reached down to Noah. Scripture then describes him: "Noah was a just man, perfect in his generations. Noah walked with God." Like Enoch before him. The order matters: grace came first, then righteousness followed. The same order governs the gospel — God's grace given freely, our walk with Him following as the response, not the cause.
blocks.es_reference: Luego viene uno de los versículos más hermosos del Antiguo Testamento: "Pero Noé halló gracia ante los ojos de Jehová". Esta es la primera aparición de la palabra gracia (hebreo chen) en la Biblia. No ganada. No merecida. Hallada. Noé no subió hasta Dios; el favor de Dios descendió hasta Noé. La Escritura entonces lo describe: "Noé, varón justo, era perfecto en sus generaciones; con Dios caminó Noé". Como Enoc antes de él. El orden importa: la gracia vino primero, luego siguió la justicia. El mismo orden gobierna el evangelio — la gracia de Dios dada libremente, nuestro caminar con Él como respuesta, no como causa.

blocks.en: 5. The Ark: God's Vessel of Salvation
blocks.es_reference: 5. El Arca: La Nave de Salvación de Dios

blocks.en: God told Noah to build an ark of gopher wood, 300 cubits long, 50 wide, 30 high — roughly 450 feet by 75 feet by 45 feet. Three decks. Pitched inside and out. One door. One window above. The dimensions are seaworthy by modern naval engineering, which has long since vindicated what skeptics once mocked. But notice the spiritual picture: there is one door. Only one. Christ Himself would later say, "I am the door. By Me, if anyone enters, he will be saved." The ark is a portrait of Christ. The whole world stood condemned, but anyone who would enter the door would live. Noah preached this message for 120 years (2 Peter 2:5) while building the ark. Eight people believed him.
blocks.es_reference: Dios le dijo a Noé que construyera un arca de madera de gofer, 300 codos de largo, 50 de ancho, 30 de alto — aproximadamente 450 pies por 75 pies por 45 pies. Tres cubiertas. Calafateada por dentro y por fuera. Una puerta. Una ventana arriba. Las dimensiones son navegables según la ingeniería naval moderna, que ha vindicado desde hace tiempo lo que los escépticos antes ridiculizaban. Pero observa la imagen espiritual: hay una puerta. Solo una. Cristo mismo diría después: "Yo soy la puerta; el que por mí entrare, será salvo". El arca es un retrato de Cristo. El mundo entero estaba condenado, pero cualquiera que entrara por la puerta viviría. Noé predicó este mensaje durante 120 años (2 Pedro 2:5) mientras construía el arca. Ocho personas le creyeron.

blocks.en: 6. The Flood: Judgment and Salvation
blocks.es_reference: 6. El Diluvio: Juicio y Salvación

blocks.en: God instructed Noah to take seven pairs of every clean animal and one pair of every unclean — a distinction made centuries before the Levitical law, showing that God's categories of clean and unclean predate the formal code. When all were aboard, "the Lord shut him in." Forty days and nights of rain. The fountains of the deep also burst open — this was not merely an atmospheric event but a cataclysmic restructuring of the earth's hydrology. The waters prevailed 150 days, covering even the highest mountains. Every living creature outside the ark perished. Yet inside the ark, eight souls were preserved. The flood is simultaneously the greatest judgment in human history and the greatest picture of salvation: those inside the vessel are safe; those outside are lost.
blocks.es_reference: Dios instruyó a Noé tomar siete pares de cada animal limpio y un par de cada inmundo — una distinción hecha siglos antes de la ley levítica, mostrando que las categorías de Dios de limpio e inmundo preceden al código formal. Cuando todos estaban a bordo, "Jehová le cerró la puerta". Cuarenta días y noches de lluvia. Las fuentes del gran abismo también se rompieron — esto no fue meramente un evento atmosférico sino una reestructuración cataclísmica de la hidrología de la tierra. Las aguas prevalecieron 150 días, cubriendo incluso los montes más altos. Toda criatura viviente fuera del arca pereció. Sin embargo, dentro del arca, ocho almas fueron preservadas. El diluvio es simultáneamente el mayor juicio en la historia humana y la mayor imagen de salvación: los que están dentro de la nave están seguros; los que están fuera están perdidos.

blocks.en: 7. The Waters Recede: A New Beginning
blocks.es_reference: 7. Las Aguas Bajan: Un Nuevo Comienzo

blocks.en: After 150 days, "God remembered Noah." Not that He had forgotten — but God's "remembering" in Hebrew always marks the beginning of decisive action. He sent a wind over the earth. The waters receded. The ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat. Noah sent out a raven, then a dove. The dove returned with an olive leaf — the first peace symbol in human imagination. After more than a year inside the ark, Noah and his family stepped out into a cleansed world. His very first act on dry ground was to build an altar and offer burnt sacrifices from the clean animals. Worship before settlement. The Lord smelled a soothing aroma and said in His heart, "I will never again curse the ground for man's sake."
blocks.es_reference: Después de 150 días, "se acordó Dios de Noé". No es que se hubiera olvidado — pero el "recordar" de Dios en hebreo siempre marca el comienzo de una acción decisiva. Envió un viento sobre la tierra. Las aguas bajaron. El arca reposó sobre los montes de Ararat. Noé envió un cuervo, luego una paloma. La paloma volvió con una hoja de olivo — el primer símbolo de paz en la imaginación humana. Después de más de un año dentro del arca, Noé y su familia salieron a un mundo limpio. Su primer acto en tierra seca fue construir un altar y ofrecer holocaustos de los animales limpios. Adoración antes de asentamiento. Jehová olió un aroma agradable y dijo en Su corazón: "No volveré más a maldecir la tierra por causa del hombre".

blocks.en: Genesis 8:21 (NKJV): "And the Lord smelled a soothing aroma. Then the Lord said in His heart, 'I will never again curse the ground for man's sake, although the imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth; nor will I again destroy every living thing as I have done.'"
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 8:21 (RVG): "Y percibió Jehová olor de suavidad; y dijo Jehová en su corazón: No volveré más a maldecir la tierra por causa del hombre; porque el intento del corazón del hombre es malo desde su juventud; ni volveré más a destruir todo viviente, como he hecho."

blocks.en: 8. The Noahic Covenant: The Bow in the Cloud
blocks.es_reference: 8. El Pacto Noético: El Arco en la Nube

blocks.en: God blessed Noah and his sons: "Be fruitful and multiply; fill the earth." Echoes of Eden. He gave new permission — Noah could now eat meat, where Adam had been vegetarian. With this came a sober new law: human life is sacred. "Whoever sheds man's blood, by man his blood shall be shed; for in the image of God He made man." Capital punishment is instituted here, grounded not in retribution but in the dignity of the divine image. Then God set His bow in the cloud — the rainbow — as the sign of the covenant. The Hebrew word for rainbow is the word for a warrior's bow. God's bow was now pointed away from the earth, drawn back toward heaven. The weapon of judgment had been laid aside. Christ would one day take that judgment Himself on a hill outside Jerusalem.
blocks.es_reference: Dios bendijo a Noé y a sus hijos: "Fructificad y multiplicaos; llenad la tierra". Ecos del Edén. Dio nuevo permiso — Noé podía ahora comer carne, donde Adán había sido vegetariano. Con esto vino una sobria nueva ley: la vida humana es sagrada. "El que derramare sangre de hombre, por el hombre su sangre será derramada; porque a imagen de Dios es hecho el hombre". La pena capital se instituye aquí, fundamentada no en venganza sino en la dignidad de la imagen divina. Luego Dios puso Su arco en la nube — el arcoíris — como señal del pacto. La palabra hebrea para arcoíris es la palabra para el arco de un guerrero. El arco de Dios estaba ahora apuntando lejos de la tierra, tensado hacia el cielo. El arma del juicio había sido depuesta. Cristo un día tomaría ese juicio sobre Sí mismo en un monte a las afueras de Jerusalén.

blocks.en: 9. Noah's Failure and the Curse on Canaan
blocks.es_reference: 9. El Fracaso de Noé y la Maldición sobre Canaán

blocks.en: Like every hero in Genesis after the Fall, Noah failed. He planted a vineyard, made wine, and lay drunk and naked in his tent. His son Ham saw him and told his brothers — likely with mockery. Shem and Japheth, by contrast, walked in backward carrying a garment to cover their father, careful not to look upon his shame. When Noah awoke, he pronounced a prophetic word: not a curse on Ham himself, but on Ham's son Canaan, whose descendants would become the Canaanites Israel would later confront. This is critically important: the curse was particular, not racial. Many later interpreters tried to twist this text to justify enslaving African peoples. The text gives no such warrant. The Canaanites spoke a Semitic language, though Genesis 10 traces Canaan's line to Ham.
blocks.es_reference: Como cada héroe en Génesis después de la Caída, Noé falló. Plantó una viña, hizo vino y yació borracho y desnudo en su tienda. Su hijo Cam lo vio y se lo dijo a sus hermanos — probablemente con burla. Sem y Jafet, en cambio, caminaron de espaldas llevando un manto para cubrir a su padre, cuidando de no mirar su vergüenza. Cuando Noé despertó, pronunció una palabra profética: no una maldición sobre Cam mismo, sino sobre el hijo de Cam, Canaán, cuyos descendientes se convertirían en los cananeos que Israel después enfrentaría. Esto es críticamente importante: la maldición fue particular, no racial. Muchos intérpretes posteriores intentaron torcer este texto para justificar la esclavización de pueblos africanos. El texto no da tal justificación. Los cananeos hablaban una lengua semítica, aunque Génesis 10 remonta el linaje de Canaán a Cam.

blocks.en: 10. The Table of Nations
blocks.es_reference: 10. La Tabla de las Naciones

blocks.en: Genesis 10 lists seventy nations descended from Noah's three sons — Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Seventy is no accident; it becomes a recurring biblical number for the nations of the world. From Japheth came the Indo-European peoples spreading north and west. From Ham came African and southwestern Asian peoples. From Shem came the Semitic peoples — Israel's line, but also Arab, Aramean, and Assyrian peoples. This chapter teaches a foundational truth: every human being on earth descends from Noah, and ultimately from Adam. There is one race — the human race. Differences of language, culture, and skin are real, but they are surface variations on a deeper unity. Racism is a denial of Genesis 10 before it is anything else.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 10 enumera setenta naciones descendientes de los tres hijos de Noé — Sem, Cam y Jafet. Setenta no es accidente; se convierte en un número bíblico recurrente para las naciones del mundo. De Jafet vinieron los pueblos indoeuropeos extendiéndose al norte y al oeste. De Cam vinieron pueblos africanos y del suroeste de Asia. De Sem vinieron los pueblos semíticos — la línea de Israel, pero también pueblos árabes, arameos y asirios. Este capítulo enseña una verdad fundamental: todo ser humano en la tierra desciende de Noé, y en última instancia de Adán. Hay una raza — la raza humana. Las diferencias de lengua, cultura y piel son reales, pero son variaciones superficiales sobre una unidad más profunda. El racismo es una negación de Génesis 10 antes que cualquier otra cosa.

blocks.en: 11. Babel: The Pride of Humanity Scattered
blocks.es_reference: 11. Babel: El Orgullo de la Humanidad Esparcido

blocks.en: The people of the earth still spoke one language. They settled in the plain of Shinar (Babylonia) and said, "Come, let us build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top is in the heavens; let us make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered abroad." Read those phrases carefully. They were doing the opposite of what God had commanded. God said, "Fill the earth." They said, "Lest we be scattered." God would later tell Abraham, "I will make your name great." They said, "Let us make a name for ourselves." This was organized rebellion — a religious project (the tower was almost certainly a ziggurat for worshipping the heavens) designed to consolidate humanity against God. So the Lord came down, confused their language, and scattered them. The scattering was judgment, but also mercy — it limits the damage human evil can do when fully unified. Babel's name (Hebrew balal, "to confuse") becomes shorthand throughout Scripture for human pride opposing God. The closing verses of Genesis 11 trace the line of Shem down to Abram — and the next great chapter of redemption begins.
blocks.es_reference: El pueblo de la tierra todavía hablaba un idioma. Se asentaron en la llanura de Sinar (Babilonia) y dijeron: "Vamos, edifiquémonos una ciudad y una torre, cuya cúspide llegue al cielo; y hagámonos un nombre, por si fuéremos esparcidos sobre la faz de toda la tierra". Lee esas frases cuidadosamente. Estaban haciendo lo opuesto a lo que Dios había mandado. Dios dijo: "Llenad la tierra". Ellos dijeron: "Por si fuéremos esparcidos". Dios después le diría a Abraham: "Engrandeceré tu nombre". Ellos dijeron: "Hagámonos un nombre". Esta era rebelión organizada — un proyecto religioso (la torre era casi con certeza un zigurat para adorar los cielos) diseñado para consolidar a la humanidad contra Dios. Entonces el Señor descendió, confundió su lengua y los dispersó. La dispersión fue juicio, pero también misericordia — limita el daño que el mal humano puede hacer cuando está totalmente unificado. El nombre Babel (hebreo balal, "confundir") se convierte en taquigrafía a lo largo de la Escritura para el orgullo humano que se opone a Dios. Los versículos finales de Génesis 11 trazan la línea de Sem hasta Abram — y el siguiente gran capítulo de redención comienza.

mc.stem: How many generations are recorded from Adam to Noah in Genesis 5?
mc.why: Correct. Genesis 5 records ten generations from Adam to Noah — a deliberate genealogy showing God preserving a line through judgment.

mc.stem: What was distinctive about Enoch in Genesis 5?
options: He walked with God and was taken without dying
mc.why: Yes. Enoch did not die — God 'took him.' Centuries before any explicit doctrine of resurrection, God hinted at life beyond the grave.

mc.stem: The phrase 'sons of God' in Genesis 6 is most naturally understood as referring to what?
mc.why: Correct. The phrase bene elohim is used elsewhere in the OT (Job 1:6) for angelic beings — and Jude and 2 Peter both seem to confirm this reading.

mc.stem: What word first appears in the Bible in connection with Noah?
mc.why: Yes. 'Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord' — the first occurrence of chen in Scripture.

mc.stem: What did Noah's father Lamech prophesy at his birth?
options: 'This one will comfort us concerning the toil of our hands'
mc.why: Correct. Lamech prophesied Noah would bring relief from the curse on the ground — and the flood reset that ground.

mc.stem: How many doors did the ark have?
mc.why: Yes. One door — pointing forward to Christ, who said, 'I am the door; if anyone enters by Me, he will be saved.'

mc.stem: Approximately how long did Noah preach while building the ark?
mc.why: Correct. 2 Peter 2:5 calls Noah a 'preacher of righteousness' during the 120 years (Genesis 6:3) before the flood.

mc.stem: How many of each clean animal did Noah take into the ark?
mc.why: Yes. Seven pairs of each clean animal, one pair of each unclean — a clean/unclean distinction predating the Levitical code.

mc.stem: How long did the floodwaters prevail over the earth?
mc.why: Correct. 150 days — though Noah and family were in the ark over a year total before stepping out.

mc.stem: What was Noah's first recorded act after leaving the ark?
options: Built an altar and offered sacrifices
mc.why: Yes. Worship before settlement. Noah's first act on cleansed ground was to build an altar.

mc.stem: What change in diet did God permit Noah that Adam had not been given?
mc.why: Correct. Adam was vegetarian (Genesis 1:29). Noah received permission to eat meat — a marker of the world's changed condition.

mc.stem: The rainbow in Genesis 9 uses what Hebrew word?
options: The word for a warrior's bow
mc.why: Yes. God's weapon of judgment was now drawn back, pointing away from the earth — a stunning image of mercy.

mc.stem: Why was Canaan, not Ham, cursed after the vineyard incident?
options: The curse was particular to Ham's son Canaan and his line, not Ham himself
mc.why: Correct. The curse was specific to Canaan's line — later the Canaanites Israel would confront. It was never a racial curse.

mc.stem: How many nations does Genesis 10 record as descended from Noah's sons?
mc.why: Yes. Seventy nations from Shem, Ham, and Japheth — a number that recurs throughout Scripture as 'the nations.'

mc.stem: What were the people at Babel trying to build?
options: A city and a tower reaching to heaven
mc.why: Correct. A city and a tower — likely a ziggurat for worshipping the heavens. Organized religious rebellion.

mc.stem: What was the people's stated motivation at Babel?
options: To make a name for themselves and avoid being scattered
mc.why: Yes. Pride and disobedience — God said 'fill the earth,' they said 'lest we be scattered.'

mc.stem: God's later promise to Abram inverts what Babel-builders said. What did God promise Abram?
mc.why: Correct. Babel said, 'Let us make a name'; God said to Abram, 'I will make your name great.' The contrast is deliberate.

mc.stem: How did God respond at Babel?
options: Confused their language and scattered them
mc.why: Yes. God confused their language. Scattering was judgment but also mercy — it limits the damage united evil can do.

mc.stem: What does 'Babel' mean in Hebrew?
mc.why: Correct. From balal, 'to confuse.' Babel becomes shorthand in Scripture for organized human pride opposing God.

mc.stem: Genesis 11 ends by tracing whose genealogy?
mc.why: Yes. Shem to Abram — setting up the next great chapter of redemption.

sa.prompt: How does the ark serve as a picture of Christ?
sa.model: The ark had one door. Christ said, 'I am the door.' Those inside the vessel were safe; those outside perished. The picture is unmistakable.

sa.prompt: What does the existence of clean and unclean animals before the Levitical law tell us?
sa.model: The categories existed centuries before Sinai, showing God's distinctions are not arbitrary code-making but reflect deeper truths about His order.

sa.prompt: Why did Noah build an altar as his first act after leaving the ark?
sa.model: Worship before settlement. Noah recognized that survival came from God, not from his own labor — gratitude and dependence preceded everything else.

sa.prompt: Explain the significance of the rainbow using the Hebrew word for a warrior's bow.
sa.model: God's weapon of judgment was now drawn back, pointing away from the earth toward heaven — a stunning picture of mercy and covenant.

sa.prompt: Why is it important to understand that the curse on Canaan was particular, not racial?
sa.model: The curse fell on Canaan's specific line, who became the Canaanites — Semitic peoples in Palestine. The text gives no warrant for race-based slavery.

sa.prompt: What does Genesis 10 teach about human unity and racism?
sa.model: Every human descends from Noah and ultimately Adam. Differences are surface variations on a deeper unity. Racism contradicts the basic biblical anthropology.

sa.prompt: Contrast the Babel-builders' words ('let us make a name for ourselves') with what God later said to Abram.
sa.model: Babel tried to seize a great name by pride; God freely gave Abram a great name by promise. What humanity grasps for, God gives to those who walk by faith.

sa.prompt: Why was the scattering at Babel both judgment and mercy?
sa.model: Judgment because it broke their rebellion; mercy because it limited how much evil a unified humanity could accomplish together.
